blocks.p: Now while they were drawing near to the gate, a company of the heavenly host came out to meet them; and the other two Shining Ones said to them, “These are the men who loved our Lord when they were in the world, and who left everything for his holy name; and he sent us to bring them, and we have brought them this far on their longed-for journey, so that they may go in and look their Redeemer in the face with joy.”

Then the heavenly host gave a great shout, saying, “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb!” [Rev. 19:9] At this time, too, several of the King’s trumpeters came out to meet them, dressed in white and shining clothing, and with sounds both melodious and loud they made the very heavens echo. These trumpeters greeted Christian and his companion with ten thousand welcomes from the world; and they did it with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.

When this was done, they surrounded them on every side: some went in front, some behind, some on the right hand, and some on the left, as if to guard them through the upper regions, sounding continually as they went, in melodious notes on high; so that the very sight of it, to anyone who could see it, was as if heaven itself had come down to meet them. So they walked on together; and as they walked, every now and then these trumpeters, with joyful sound, mixing their music with looks and gestures, kept showing Christian and his brother how welcome they were into their company, and how glad they were to come and meet them. And now these two men were, as it were, in heaven before they reached it, swallowed up with the sight of angels and the sound of their melodious notes. Here also they had the city itself in view, and they thought they heard all its bells ringing to welcome them. But above all were the warm and joyful thoughts they had of living there themselves, in such company, and that forever and ever. Oh, what tongue or pen could express their glorious joy! And so they came up to the gate.

Now when they had come up to the gate, there was written over it in letters of gold: “Blessed are those who do his commandments, so that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter through the gates into the city.” [Rev. 22:14]

Then I saw in my dream that the Shining Men told them to call at the gate. When they did, some looked down from above the gate: Enoch, Moses, Elijah, and others. And it was said to them, “These pilgrims have come from the City of Destruction for the love they bear to the King of this place.” Then the pilgrims each handed in the certificate they had received at the beginning; and these were carried in to the King. When he had read them, he said, “Where are the men?”
“They are standing outside the gate,” they answered.
Then the King commanded the gate to be opened, “so that the righteous nation,” he said, “which keeps the truth, may enter in.” [Isa. 26:2]

Now I saw in my dream that these two men went in at the gate; and as they entered, they were transfigured, and were dressed in clothing that shone like gold. There were also those who met them with harps and crowns and gave them to them: the harps for praising, and the crowns as a sign of honor. Then I heard in my dream that all the bells in the city rang again for joy, and that it was said to them, “ENTER INTO THE JOY OF YOUR LORD.” I also heard the men themselves singing with a loud voice, “BLESSING AND HONOR AND GLORY AND POWER BE TO HIM WHO SITS ON THE THRONE, AND TO THE LAMB, FOREVER AND EVER.” [Rev. 5:13]

Now, just as the gates were opened to let the men in, I looked in after them; and the City shone like the sun. The streets also were paved with gold, and in them walked many people with crowns on their heads, palms in their hands, and golden harps to sing praises with.

There were also some among them who had wings, and they answered one another without ceasing, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.” [Rev. 4:8] And after that they shut the gates; and when I had seen it, I wished I were among them.

Now while I was gazing at all these things, I turned my head to look back, and I saw Ignorance come up to the riverside. But he soon got over, and with not half the difficulty the other two men had met. For it happened that there was a ferryman in that place at the time, one Vain-hope, who helped him over in his boat. So he, like the others I had seen, climbed the hill to come up to the gate; only he came alone, and no one met him with the least encouragement. When he had come up to the gate, he looked up at the writing above it, and then began to knock, supposing that he would quickly be let in. But the men who looked over the top of the gate asked him, “Where have you come from, and what do you want?”
“I have eaten and drunk in the presence of the King,” he answered, “and he has taught in our streets.”
Then they asked him for his certificate, so that they could go in and show it to the King. He fumbled inside his coat for one, and found none.
“Have you none?” they said. But the man did not answer a word.

So they told the King; but he would not come down to see him. Instead he commanded the two Shining Ones who had led Christian and Hopeful to the city to go out and take Ignorance, and bind him hand and foot, and take him away. Then they took him up and carried him through the air to the door that I had seen in the side of the hill, and put him in there.
Then I saw that there was a way to hell even from the gates of heaven, as well as from the City of Destruction.
So I awoke, and saw that it was a dream.
